title: Stalk tensor comparison for two presheaves of modules
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $R$ a presheaf of commutative rings, $x\in X$, and $F,G$ presheaves of $R$-modules (the restrictions are semilinear over those of $R$). Let $P(U)=F(U)\otimes_{R(U)}G(U)$ with tensor restrictions [def-pur-presheaf-tensor-product]. With stalks and their induced scalar actions as in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], there is an $R_x$-linear isomorphism $e:P_x\xrightarrow{\sim}F_x\otimes_{R_x}G_x$ such that $e((s\otimes t)_x)=s_x\otimes t_x$ for every neighborhood $U$ of $x$, $s\in F(U)$, and $t\in G(U)$.

proof.text: For a neighborhood U of x the pairing (s,t) ↦ s_x tensor t_x is additive in each variable and balanced by germ_smul. TensorProduct.liftAddHom gives an additive map on the section tensor product. The tensor restriction formula and germ_res_apply give a cocone on the neighborhood diagram; colimit.desc produces p:(F tensor_p G)_x → F_x tensor_{R_x} G_x, with the asserted pure-tensor germ formula.

proof.text: Represent m∈F_x and n∈G_x on a common neighborhood U. Set b(m,n) to the germ of their section tensor. If another pair represents the same germs, germ_eq gives two smaller neighborhoods on which the factor restrictions agree. Intersect them; presheaf composition and tensor restriction show that both tensor germs agree. The construction is independent of the representatives.

proof.text: For additivity in either variable, choose representatives for the three vectors on a common neighborhood using exists_le_germ_eq. Apply sectionwise additivity of tensor products and of germs. For stalk-ring linearity, represent the scalar first and restrict both vector representatives into its neighborhood; germ_smul and smul_tmul or tmul_smul give the two linearity equations. This yields a bilinear map β:F_x →ₗ[R_x] G_x →ₗ[R_x] (F tensor_p G)_x.

proof.text: Let q be TensorProduct.lift β. The identity q(p(z))=z follows by representing z as a germ of a section tensor and applying tensor induction. For p(q(z))=z, use tensor induction and represent the two factors of each stalk pure tensor on a common neighborhood. Both identities follow from the germ formulas. Since q is linear and inverse to p, p is linear: apply injectivity of q to p(a z)=a p(z), then use q linear and q∘p=id. LinearEquiv.ofBijective and toModuleIso give the required isomorphism.
